question.text: The quick ratio (acid test) excludes which item from current assets?

answer.text: Inventory — because it may not be quickly convertible to cash

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 174), Quick Ratio = (Cash + Receivables + Investments) / Current Liabilities. Inventory is excluded because it cannot always be quickly converted to cash. The Trap: Cash, trade receivables, and short-term investments are treated as liquid current assets. Inventory takes time to sell and may have to be discounted. Note: A higher quick ratio indicates better availability of liquid assets to meet immediate short-term obligations (page 175).
